Hi Aisha, Tom —

Appended below is a concise phased switchover proposal and the high-level backout criteria. I've looped in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (CS) to add technical thresholds and operational steps. We also attached a checklist spreadsheet for your ops runbook.

Summary (high level):
- Canary day (T+0): 2% of production traffic routed to Redwood hosted inference cluster for 4 hours; health checks every 2 minutes.
- Ramp (T+1 to T+3): 2 -> 10% (T+1), 10 -> 40% (T+2), 40 -> 100% (T+3) subject to gating.
- Gating: error rate increase >0.5% absolute, median 95th latency exceeding SLO by 25%, or model quality regression on acceptance prompts -> pause and investigate.
- Backout: automatic rollback to previous routing within 10 minutes if any gating condition persists after 2 consecutive checks or manual rollback on approval from Fiducia ops lead.

Next steps: Karthik to provide exact health-check URLs, log retention for the canary window, and KV/cache sync advice. Marissa will propose post-switchover validation prompts and the SLA for quick fixes.

Hi all — adding the technical thresholds and operational steps. I kept it pragmatic for your runbook.

Operational details (technical):
- Canary selection: 5% of API keys (randomized) + traffic pin to a small host pool. Prefer early-morning low-traffic windows for T+0.
- Latency gates: 95th percentile token latency > 1.25x baseline OR median inference time > 600ms triggers hold.
- Error gates: HTTP 5xx or model inference exceptions > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline.
- Replication/data sync: For customers using private embeddings storage, recommend final data sync window of 30 minutes prior to T+3 cutover and an incremental sync every 5 minutes during ramp.
- KV cache warming: pre-warm top 5k keys using warmed-prefix job; target cache-hit ratio > 70% before >40% traffic.
- Log & observability: stream canary logs to your SIEM + our console with 1-hour retention for canary period, full retention post-day 2 per contract.

Suggested manual approval points:
- Pre-T+0: Fiducia ops signoff on traffic selection and rollback contact.
- Pre-T+3 (40%->100%): joint go/no-go after 24-hour stability window OR automatic progression if no gating conditions.

I attached a short PDF with canary selection heuristics and sample health-check endpoints.

Attachment: 20260831-canary-selection-and-healthchecks.pdf

— Karthik

Tom —

Short answers and attached playbook. See included rollback-playbook.txt for the step-by-step runbook. Quick summary:

1) Replication lag: we recommend refusing requests when DB replication lag > 5 seconds for synchronous features; for eventual-style reads, set soft-degradation where read requests hit cached snapshot and writes are queued.

2) Rollback SLA: routing revert is target <= 10 minutes for automated rollback; manual rollback target is <= 30 minutes after confirmation from Fiducia ops lead. Primary contact for manual rollback: Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwood.ai) with Karthik (karthik_iyer@redwood.ai) as technical runbook lead.

3) Post-backout verification: the playbook includes a 12-point checklist (health endpoints, sample acceptance prompts, token-level error sampling, reconciled telemetry). We also provide a pre-made script (in the drive link) you can run against canary traces to validate.

If this meets your needs we'd ask for a formal sign-off (reply OK with date/time) to include in our SOW appendix.

Thanks — attaching final playbook and adding Sean from legal to the loop for the change advisory items.

Attachments: 20260903-rollback-playbook.txt
